neighbours.label: a preposition giving spatial or range extent after a verb of continuing/extending ('continue for', 'extend throughout', 'at which')
fire: The cave passages stretch for nearly two kilometres under the hill.
These coal seams extend for hundreds of metres below the valley.
The old wall runs for several miles along the northern border.
The reef continues for many kilometres along the eastern coast.
Cracks in the ice spread for dozens of metres across the lake.
The sandstone ridge stretches for about forty miles to the south.
Tunnels beneath the castle extend for a great distance under the town.
The fault line runs for hundreds of kilometres through the desert.

These coal seams were mined by hand below the valley.
The old wall was built by soldiers along the northern border.
The reef is home to colourful fish along the eastern coast.
Cracks in the ice frightened the skaters on the lake.
